text: Write a program that prints one pattern under several agreements, closing the loop on Chapter 1. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: System.out.println("as byte : " + ___);      // narrow to eight bits
System.out.println("as char : " + ___);      // read as a character
explanation: Verified: 200, -56, È, and c8. Chapter 1 argued this on paper; here it is, four lines of Java, four readings of one number. Notice that the casts are not conversions in any meaningful sense — nothing about the pattern changes — they are instructions to the compiler about which agreement to apply when printing. That is what a cast between primitive types largely is.
